samples.input:
Use a surfaceId of 'main'. Generate a 'createSurface' message to describe the following UI:

A vertical list with:
- Dog breed information
- Dog generator

The dog breed information is a card, which contains a title “Famous Dog breeds”, a header image, and a horizontal list of images of different dog breeds (using a 'List' component). The list information should be in the data model at /breeds.

The dog generator is another card which is a form that generates a fictional dog breed with a description
- Title
- Description text explaining what it is
- Dog breed name (text input)
- Number of legs (number input)
- Button called “Generate” which takes the data above and generates a new dog description
- Skills (ChoicePicker component, variant 'multipleSelection')
- A divider
- A section which shows the generated content

messages.content:
You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.


## Component Catalog Signatures:
- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)
  - :url: The URL of the audio to be played.
  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Button :child :variant? :action :weight? :checks?)
  - :child: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :variant: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Card :child :weight?)
  - :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (CheckBox :label :value :weight? :checks?)
  - :label: The text to display next to the checkbox.
  - :value: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (ChoicePicker :label? :variant? :options :value :displayStyle? :filterable? :weight? :checks?)

  - :label: The label for the group of options.
  - :variant: A hint for how the choice picker should be displayed and behave. Must be one of: 'multipleSelection', 'mutuallyExclusive'
  - :options: The list of available options to choose from.
  - :value: The list of currently selected values. This should be bound to a string array in the data model.
  - :displayStyle: The display style of the component. Must be one of: 'checkbox', 'chips'
  - :filterable: If true, displays a search input to filter the options.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

content.summary:
**UI Construction Process: A Deep Dive into A2UI Atom S-Expressions**

Alright, let's break down this A2UI Atom UI creation step-by-step. The goal is to build a UI with two cards: "Dog breed information" and "Dog generator," all within a 'main' surface and rooted with an element with ID 'root'. The primary constraint is the strict adherence to A2UI Atom's grammar, specifically inline nesting and the complete absence of explicit IDs, as well as the need to represent tree structures using a parenthesis-based S-Expression format. No flat lists of elements, only proper tree hierarchies as defined by the A2UI spec.

First, understanding the *strict* requirements here is critical. We can't simply use the provided catalog description without taking into account the explicit grammar rules. We must nest elements inline as children of Column/Row/Card and never use any IDs except for the default 'root'.

The root is the first element of the expression. So, we'll start with a `Column`. The prompt's requirement for a root element with ID 'root', while somewhat contradictory to the grammar's lack of explicit IDs, seems to be handled implicitly. Thus, the system treats the root element as having ID 'root'.

Next, constructing the UI tree by nesting and using the appropriate data attributes. We use a vertical `Column` as the root to contain two `Card` components, one for "Dog breed information" and the other for "Dog generator." Each `Card` will then contain its own nested structure.

The "Dog breed information" card will include a title, a header image, and a horizontal list of dog breed images, populated from a data model at `/breeds`. This list will use a `List` component with a `template` to generate `Image` components for each breed in the data. Here the rules for `List` with a `template` ensure we don't define the children via ID.

The "Dog generator" card will consist of a form with `TextField` inputs for breed name and leg count, a `ChoicePicker` for skills, a "Generate" `Button`, a `Divider`, and a section to display the generated description. I'm choosing to define data in the s-expression, initializing it, setting defaults, and using an `Event` to represent the button's action. The generated description output will be dynamically populated from the input form by binding to `$/generated/description`.

The most interesting thing is resolving the conflicts between the catalog descriptions which seem to be boilerplate from some other system and the extremely clear grammar rules of A2UI Atom. We need to remember that the S-expression format is designed for tree-like nesting, which is the key to creating our UI. The structure will be:
```lisp
(Column (Card (Column ...)) (Card (Column ...)))
```
All children MUST be positional or defined as a keyword argument (e.g. `:child` or `:children`).

The data model will be initialized within the top-level `Column` using the `data` keyword to set initial values for dog breed data, skill options, and form fields.

Now let's verify each element's signature:
-   `Column`: `:children` as keyword arguments.
-   `Card`:  `:child` as a keyword argument.
-   `List`: `:children`, `:direction`
-   `Text`: `:text`, `:variant`.
-   `Image`: `:url`, `:description`, `:variant`.
-   `TextField`: `:label`, `:value`, `:placeholder`, `:variant`.
-   `ChoicePicker`: `:label`, `:variant`, `:options`, `:value`, `:displayStyle`.
-   `Button`: `:child`, `:variant`, `:action`.
-   `Divider`: `:axis`.

The action for the Generate button will be an `Event`, bound to the generated dog description. The goal is to make sure we've got the correct S-expression to express a rich form that includes the list of dog images, form field inputs, and the "Generate" button. This will be an elegant solution that is easy to understand in this format. The full output includes initial data, the two main cards, and has been reviewed for full conformance. We should have a working S-Expression UI.

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column
  :children [
    (data
      $/breeds [
        (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1" :name "Golden Retriever")
        (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1552053831-71594a27632d" :name "Labrador")
        (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1537151625747-7ae87041ee87" :name "Beagle")
      ]
      $/skills_options ["Super Jump" "Lava Resistance" "Telepathy" "Speedy Fetch" "Sleep Anywhere"]
      $/form/name ""
      $/form/legs "4"
      $/form/skills []
      $/generated/description "Enter details and click 'Generate' to see your custom breed description here!"
    )
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
          (Image :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1" :description "Header Dog" :variant "header")
          (List
            :direction "horizontal"
            :children (template :item breed
              (Image :url $/breed/url :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
            )
          )
        ]
      )
    )
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Fictional Dog Generator" :variant "body")
          (Text :text "Create your own unique dog breed by filling out the details below." :variant "caption")
          (TextField :label "Dog Breed Name" :value $/form/name :placeholder "e.g., Cyber Hound" :variant "shortText")
          (TextField :label "Number of Legs" :value $/form/legs :placeholder "4" :variant "number")
          (ChoicePicker
            :label "Skills"
            :variant "multipleSelection"
            :options $/skills_options
            :value $/form/skills
            :displayStyle "chips"
          )
          (Button
            :child (Text :text "Generate")
            :variant "primary"
            :action (Event "generate_dog" :name $/form/name :legs $/form/legs :skills $/form/skills)
          )
          (Divider :axis "horizontal")
          (Text :text "Generated Breed Details" :variant "body")
          (Text :text $/generated/description :variant "body")
        ]
      )
    )
  ]
)
</a2ui>

**UI Construction Process: A Deep Dive into A2UI Atom S-Expressions**

Alright, let's break down this A2UI Atom UI creation step-by-step. The goal is to build a UI with two cards: "Dog breed information" and "Dog generator," all within a 'main' surface and rooted with an element with ID 'root'. The primary constraint is the strict adherence to A2UI Atom's grammar, specifically inline nesting and the complete absence of explicit IDs, as well as the need to represent tree structures using a parenthesis-based S-Expression format. No flat lists of elements, only proper tree hierarchies as defined by the A2UI spec.

First, understanding the *strict* requirements here is critical. We can't simply use the provided catalog description without taking into account the explicit grammar rules. We must nest elements inline as children of Column/Row/Card and never use any IDs except for the default 'root'.

The root is the first element of the expression. So, we'll start with a `Column`. The prompt's requirement for a root element with ID 'root', while somewhat contradictory to the grammar's lack of explicit IDs, seems to be handled implicitly. Thus, the system treats the root element as having ID 'root'.

Next, constructing the UI tree by nesting and using the appropriate data attributes. We use a vertical `Column` as the root to contain two `Card` components, one for "Dog breed information" and the other for "Dog generator." Each `Card` will then contain its own nested structure.

The "Dog breed information" card will include a title, a header image, and a horizontal list of dog breed images, populated from a data model at `/breeds`. This list will use a `List` component with a `template` to generate `Image` components for each breed in the data. Here the rules for `List` with a `template` ensure we don't define the children via ID.

The "Dog generator" card will consist of a form with `TextField` inputs for breed name and leg count, a `ChoicePicker` for skills, a "Generate" `Button`, a `Divider`, and a section to display the generated description. I'm choosing to define data in the s-expression, initializing it, setting defaults, and using an `Event` to represent the button's action. The generated description output will be dynamically populated from the input form by binding to `$/generated/description`.

The most interesting thing is resolving the conflicts between the catalog descriptions which seem to be boilerplate from some other system and the extremely clear grammar rules of A2UI Atom. We need to remember that the S-expression format is designed for tree-like nesting, which is the key to creating our UI. The structure will be:
```lisp
(Column (Card (Column ...)) (Card (Column ...)))
```
All children MUST be positional or defined as a keyword argument (e.g. `:child` or `:children`).

The data model will be initialized within the top-level `Column` using the `data` keyword to set initial values for dog breed data, skill options, and form fields.

Now let's verify each element's signature:

content.summary:
**Login Form UI Construction**

Alright, let's break this down step-by-step. The objective is to build a login form on the 'main' surface. We need a header, two text fields (username and password), a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button with an associated action. The core principle here is to use A2UI's S-expression format, adhering to the given grammar and component catalog.

First, I'm setting up the data initialization. This is done with the `data` expression, defining initial values for username, password, and rememberMe in the `$/login` path.  This ensures the data model is ready to be bound to UI components.

Next, the root element. Since we are building a vertical layout for the login form components, a `Column` with `id: "root"` is the natural choice.  I've opted for `:align "center"` and `:justify "center"` on the `Column` to center the form elements. I'm taking care to use only attributes specified in the `Column` catalog, which means no CSS or arbitrary styling.

Now, let's build the UI components. I'll add the `# Login` header using `Text` with Markdown formatting.  Then, two `TextField` components, one for username and the other for password.  The password field has the `obscured` variant to hide input.  Both `TextField` components have labels, placeholders, and their values are bound to the data model using `$/login/username` and `$/login/password`.  Following this, a `CheckBox` for the "Remember Me" option with its value bound to `$/login/rememberMe`.

The key part is the "Sign In" `Button` component.  It's critical to pay attention to the component catalog.  I'm using the `Button`'s `:child` to nest the `Text` component "Sign In."  The `:child` property allows me to nest the text "Sign In" directly inside the button as a child.  The `:variant` attribute is set to "primary" for visual style. The crucial thing is the button's `:action`.  We need an event to trigger on click, so I'll create an `Event` with "login" as the name, which the user requested. The `Event` takes a `:context` which is a map containing the username, password, and rememberMe status, sourced from the data model.  This structure is both clean and in alignment with the grammar.

Finally, ensuring everything is properly nested, adhering to the tree-like structure mandated by the rules, and no extraneous IDs or flat structures, and that it all fits the constraints of the prompt, the grammar, and the catalog.

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root" :align "center" :justify "center"
  (data $/login (:username "" :password "" :rememberMe false))
  (Text :text "# Login")
  (TextField :label "Username" :value $/login/username :placeholder "Enter username" :variant "shortText")
  (TextField :label "Password" :value $/login/password :placeholder "Enter password" :variant "obscured")
  (CheckBox :label "Remember Me" :value $/login/rememberMe)
  (Button :child (Text :text "Sign In") :variant "primary" :action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))))
</a2ui>

**Login Form UI Construction**

Alright, let's break this down step-by-step. The objective is to build a login form on the 'main' surface. We need a header, two text fields (username and password), a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button with an associated action. The core principle here is to use A2UI's S-expression format, adhering to the given grammar and component catalog.

First, I'm setting up the data initialization. This is done with the `data` expression, defining initial values for username, password, and rememberMe in the `$/login` path.  This ensures the data model is ready to be bound to UI components.

Next, the root element. Since we are building a vertical layout for the login form components, a `Column` with `id: "root"` is the natural choice.  I've opted for `:align "center"` and `:justify "center"` on the `Column` to center the form elements. I'm taking care to use only attributes specified in the `Column` catalog, which means no CSS or arbitrary styling.

Now, let's build the UI components. I'll add the `# Login` header using `Text` with Markdown formatting.  Then, two `TextField` components, one for username and the other for password.  The password field has the `obscured` variant to hide input.  Both `TextField` components have labels, placeholders, and their values are bound to the data model using `$/login/username` and `$/login/password`.  Following this, a `CheckBox` for the "Remember Me" option with its value bound to `$/login/rememberMe`.

The key part is the "Sign In" `Button` component.  It's critical to pay attention to the component catalog.  I'm using the `Button`'s `:child` to nest the `Text` component "Sign In."  The `:child` property allows me to nest the text "Sign In" directly inside the button as a child.  The `:variant` attribute is set to "primary" for visual style. The crucial thing is the button's `:action`.  We need an event to trigger on click, so I'll create an `Event` with "login" as the name, which the user requested. The `Event` takes a `:context` which is a map containing the username, password, and rememberMe status, sourced from the data model.  This structure is both clean and in alignment with the grammar.

Finally, ensuring everything is properly nested, adhering to the tree-like structure mandated by the rules, and no extraneous IDs or flat structures, and that it all fits the constraints of the prompt, the grammar, and the catalog.

Create a UI on surface 'main' for a user settings page. Use a Tabs component with two tabs: "Profile" and "# Notifications". The "Profile" tab should contain a simple column with a text field for the user's name. The "# Notifications" tab should contain a checkbox for "Enable email notifications". Also, include a Modal component. **UI Construction Deep Dive**

Okay, here's the breakdown of how I'm approaching this user settings UI. The goal is to build a structure that strictly adheres to the A2UI Atom Output Contract, paying close attention to the nuances of component nesting and avoiding any forbidden elements. I'm focusing on surface 'main' as specified.

First, I'll structure the overall UI with a root `Column` component. I'm carefully considering whether to include an `:id "root"` attribute. The instructions *suggest* this for the root but also *prohibit* explicit IDs. Given the strict nature of the output contract's constraints, I'm interpreting "ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'" as a system-level requirement that doesn't violate the prohibition against *explicit* IDs. I will, however, include `:id "root"` on the root container, as it's a common practice.

Next, I have a `Tabs` component. The requirement specifies "Profile" and "# Notifications" tabs. The tab structure uses a list-like format: `(:title "Profile" :child (Column ...))`. I'm confirming that the `Tabs`' children, the actual content of each tab, are defined inline, which aligns with the Atom Contract.

Inside the "Profile" tab, I'll place a `Column` containing a `TextField` for the user's name. I'm using the `:value` for data binding (e.g., `$/profile/name`) and also initializing the value with a default using `(data ...)`.

The "# Notifications" tab also gets a `Column`, but this time it includes a `CheckBox` for enabling email notifications. Again, I'm using data binding with `/notifications/email` and also initializing the data.

I'm including a `Divider` for clear separation between the main tab content and the deletion action.

Now comes the "Delete Account" modal. A `Button` labeled "Delete Account" will serve as the modal's `:trigger`. This is a bit tricky, but I can nest it inline. The modal's `:content` will be another `Column` containing the confirmation text and a `Row` to hold the "Confirm Deletion" and "Cancel" buttons. The event handlers are defined with (Event ...)

Crucially, I'm making sure to define child components (like the `Text` labels within the buttons and modal content) *inline*, as positional arguments within their respective parent components. I'm interpreting the component catalog instruction to not define children inline as a legacy rule, with the explicit contract's guidance overriding it.

I'm also paying close attention to component signatures to ensure all properties are valid. Everything needs to be nested directly, no intermediate IDs, and no flat lists. This is a crucial element that I will be carefully checking.

The root of this expression will be wrapped with `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`.

I'll finalize with a thorough review. All elements must follow correct lisp s-expression.

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/profile/name "" $/notifications/email true)
  (Text :text "User Settings")
  (Tabs :tabs [
    (:title "Profile" :child (Column (TextField :label "Name" :value $/profile/name :placeholder "Enter your name" :variant "shortText")))
    (:title "# Notifications" :child (Column (CheckBox :label "Enable email notifications" :value $/notifications/email)))
  ])
  (Divider :axis "horizontal")
  (Modal
    :trigger (Button :child (Text :text "Delete Account") :variant "primary" :action (Event "open_delete_modal"))
    :content (Column
      (Text :text "Are you sure you want to delete your account? This action cannot be undone." :variant "body")
      (Row
        (Button :child (Text :text "Confirm Deletion") :variant "primary" :action (Event "confirm_delete"))
        (Button :child (Text :text "Cancel") :variant "borderless" :action (Event "cancel_delete"))
      )
    )
  )
)
</a2ui>
